chapter: Traditional style, ragtime orchestra and closing questions
title: The ragtime orchestra: is it jazz?
summary: They discuss the New Orleans Ragtime Orchestra, reading versus improvising, and why Wood finds it a legitimate extension of the tradition.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well, I mean, to stick it to the ragtime orchestra, do you think of them as a jazz band?
Well, again, you're getting kind of technical, and I guess no, not really, you know, that it's a dance orchestra. Well, jazz is not ragtime, or is it? I don't know. I don't know.
I mean, the thing is that I'm just wondering about it.
What makes jazz?
They're sitting there reading a lot of the time.
Yeah. Well, I used to, some of the brass bands that played in the street used to read. They would have music mounted on their music stands on their home. But not to that extent. No, no.
I mean, this seems to me to be a very different band, and it achieves a very different sound.
Yeah.
And they've gone back and dug out things. Do you feel like they're copying records?
No.
I don't feel that either.
I don't feel that. And I think that, you know, that's what they're doing is a very legitimate sort of extension of an earlier musical tradition.
Yeah.

And I find that it's very enjoyable, but it's certainly not the brass band tradition, and it's not certainly a long, long ways from a Bourbon Street sort of jazz set, that kind of tradition. But it's, and I'm not a jazz historian, and you are, and you can put that, you know, ragtime orchestra in its proper context and proper setting.
Well, it's your reaction to it that I'm getting at. Yeah. Yeah.

Well, it falls within this sort of, you know, perimeter of things that I like, is that it is direct and accessible, and it is not frantic, and they don't play a lot of dissident chords, and they play in tune pretty much. That's good. Well, we could overlook a few that.
Go ahead.

But it has that certain sort of accessible restrained quality about it. At the same time, it flows very freely, and it's open, and it's in many ways very joyous. And now I find that all that's very appealing. Very appealing, indeed.
Well, I just wondered if you noticed how much improvising there was.
Well, not a lot, and they don't do a lot of solo work either, do they?
Yeah. It strikes me that they have a few tunes which they play, which are entirely played by here. Yeah. But they didn't do much of that Sunday. Yeah.
Do they play as a group fairly regularly, or is it kind of unusual for them to come together and do a concert like this?
It's unusual, and they would go on a tour and then play regularly.
Yeah.

But I think they do, on the whole, put a New Orleans interpretation on things. Sure. You know, it's not just the reading the music, because there are other bands that read those same arrangements, and they come out.
Come out differently.
Oh, very differently.
Yeah. Not going to be.
